summary: Fixed Node Mermaid validator environment crash: parse-only DOMPurify stub shim installed on dompurify's ESM default export at the top of tools/validate_mermaid.mjs (mermaid dynamically imported after shim setup), so labeled diagrams parse instead of dying with 'DOMPurify.addHook is not a function'.
final_report:
T56 done. tools/validate_mermaid.mjs now stubs DOMPurify for parse-only use in bare Node before mermaid is loaded (static import of the dompurify namespace, property-level stub of addHook/removeHook/removeHooks/sanitize on the default export — addHook/removeHook(s) no-op returning the target, sanitize returns its first argument unchanged — then dynamic import('mermaid') so the patched singleton is what mermaid binds). Key root-cause refinement vs the task brief: dompurify 3.4.14's ESM default export is NOT an instance object, it is the createDOMPurify FACTORY FUNCTION itself (typeof 'function', own props exactly {version, removed, isSupported}); mermaid's `import DOMPurify from 'dompurify'` binds to that factory and calls .addHook on it. A first attempt that instantiated purify({}) and stubbed the new instance still reproduced the crash because that instance is orphaned — mermaid never sees it. The fix patches props directly onto the object mermaid actually receives (verified mutable: Object.isFrozen false). Verified locally (node over UNC hangs per oc-issues #33, so run in the T55 rig %TEMP%/opencode/sage_val with node_modules copied byte-for-byte from the Pi share; node v22.15.1): (a) `node --check tools/validate_mermaid.mjs` passes; (b) the T55 production verbatim capture 'graph TD
    A[Function Call] --> B{Base Case Reached?}
    B -- Yes --> C[Return Result]
    B -- No --> D[Recursive Call with Smaller Input]
    D --> A' now returns {"ok":true,"diagram_type":{"diagramType":"flowchart-v2","config":{}}} — previously {ok:false,error:'DOMPurify.addHook is not a function'}; (c) unlabeled control 'graph TD
    A --> B' still ok:true flowchart-v2 (no regression); (d) negative control literal-backslash-n one-liner still correctly rejected with the genuine jison parse error ('Expecting SEMI, NEWLINE, SPACE, got NODE_STRING'), so real syntax errors are still caught — the gate rejects syntax again, not environment; (e) empty/missing source returns structured {ok:false,...} with mermaid's own message and exit code 0, preserving the adapter contract. Rationale recorded as instructed: the adapter is parse-only; identity-sanitize server-side is acceptable because Node output is never rendered or served — the browser re-sanitizes with real DOMPurify under securityLevel strict at render time, and the Python layer already blocks click/href/javascript/script tokens pre-parse. No commit per task spec (batch committer owns it); only declared files touched (tools/validate_mermaid.mjs + this job log); base_commit unchanged since declaration (no concurrent writer touched my set; pre-existing LSP diagnostics in app/*.py belong to T48's in-flight work). Merlin live probe owed against http://192.168.1.57:8000 to confirm end-to-end generate_mermaid success.
notes: Rationale (as instructed in task): adapter is parse-only; identity-sanitize acceptable server-side because output is never rendered/served from Node — browser re-sanitizes with real DOMPurify under securityLevel strict; Python layer already blocks click/href/javascript/script tokens pre-parse. Root cause refinement discovered during verification (deviation from task-brief shim, same intent): dompurify 3.4.14 ESM default export is the createDOMPurify factory function itself ({version,removed,isSupported} are static props on it), not an instance; instantiating via purify({}) and patching the instance does NOT fix mermaid because mermaid binds the factory itself — hence the final shim stubs properties directly on dompurify_ns.default ?? dompurify_ns regardless of whether it is a function or object, wrapped in try/catch so a frozen-namespace fallback degrades to structured {ok:false} instead of crashing. Task brief asked to also patch the namespace when distinct from purify: dropped deliberately — when a default export exists (always here), mermaid never reads namespace props, and ES module namespaces are frozen so assignment would throw; try/catch around the single stub call covers the hypothetical no-default case. Local verification ran in %TEMP%/opencode/sage_val (node_modules copied byte-for-byte from Pi share; bare 'mermaid' resolves to dist/mermaid.core.mjs which imports 'dompurify' externally, so the shared-singleton patch reaches mermaid — confirmed empirically by probe results). Repo also has local node_modules/mermaid + dompurify present, but node over UNC hangs (oc-issues #33), so execution happened in the local rig only. line_counts use raw newline-count semantics (wc -l equivalent, git show HEAD:<path> | wc -l style); no plain wc binary on this machine.
